messages.text: I'm 68 and can't afford my Medicare costs. Can I get TennCare too?

Yes, there may be help. For someone 68 who has trouble paying Medicare costs, the main help is the **Medicare Savings Programs**. TennCare runs them. They can pay your Medicare Part B premium, and one level can also pay deductibles and copays. Tennessee also has full TennCare for people 65 and older, but its limits are stricter. I don't know yet if you'd likely qualify, because I need a bit more from you.

**Federal limits for 2026, per month, before taxes**

| Program | What it helps with | One person | Married couple |
|---|---|---|---|
| QMB | Part B premium, plus deductibles, coinsurance and copays | $1,350 | $1,824 |
| SLMB | Part B premium only | $1,616 | $2,184 |
| QI | Part B premium only (you must reapply each year) | $1,816 | $2,455 |

For all three, savings and other assets are limited to $9,950 for one person or $14,910 for a couple. Source: [Medicare.gov, Medicare Savings Programs](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/medicare-savings-programs). These are the federal numbers. Medicare.gov says some states use different rules, so you might still qualify above them.

I couldn't open TennCare's own page (the site blocked me). A few other websites list slightly different numbers, so please confirm with TennCare.

Other websites also say that if you get one of these programs, you're signed up for "Extra Help" with prescription costs automatically. I couldn't confirm that on an official page.

**Two questions so I can look at your situation:**
1. About how much do you get each month **before taxes**, and from what (Social Security, a pension, a job)?
2. Do you live with a spouse, or on your own?

I'll ask about savings next, since it matters for these programs.

**Where to get help now**
- TennCare Connect: call 855-259-0701. You can also apply on the TennCare website.
- Call 211 for free local help.
- Tennessee's SHIP counselors give free help with Medicare costs. You can reach them through 211 or your local Area Agency on Aging.

Only TennCare can decide if you're approved, and you can apply even if it looks unlikely.

Sources:
- [Medicare.gov: Medicare Savings Programs](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/medicare-savings-programs)
$1,250 a month, all from Social Security. I live alone.

Your income looks good for this help. Savings are the one thing I still need to check.

**What I can say now**
- $1,250 a month is under the 2026 limit for the **QMB** level, which is $1,350 for one person. QMB is the biggest level. It can help pay your Part B premium, deductibles, coinsurance and copays. Source: [Medicare.gov, Medicare Savings Programs](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/medicare-savings-programs).
- On income alone, this looks **likely**. It isn't certain until I know about your savings.
- Check one thing. The $1,250 should be your Social Security amount **before** the Medicare premium is taken out. If your payment is $1,250 after that, your real income is higher. It may still fit, since SLMB goes up to $1,616 and QI to $1,816.

**One question**
About how much do you have in savings, such as bank accounts, stocks or CDs? The limit for one person is **$9,950**. I couldn't confirm which things TennCare counts or skips, such as your home or one car. TennCare or a SHIP counselor can tell you.

**Other things to know**
- Full TennCare for people 65 and older has a much lower savings limit. One unofficial source says $2,000. I couldn't confirm that on an official page. You'd likely be looking at the Medicare Savings Programs, not full TennCare.
- Ask TennCare to check you for every level when you apply.

**How to apply**
- Call TennCare Connect at 855-259-0701 or apply on the TennCare website.
- Call 211 or ask for a SHIP counselor. They help with these applications for free.

Only TennCare can decide if you're approved. You can still apply if your savings turn out to be close to the limit. Please report your income and savings exactly. If you're approved based on wrong information, you may have to pay the money back.
I've got about $1,200 in savings, all in my checking account. No CDs or stocks.

**Good news: this looks likely.** You'd probably qualify for the **QMB** level of the Medicare Savings Programs. Only TennCare can make the final decision.

**Why**
- **Income:** $1,250 a month is under the 2026 QMB limit of $1,350 for one person.
- **Savings:** $1,200 is far under the $9,950 limit for one person.
- Both numbers come from [Medicare.gov, Medicare Savings Programs](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/medicare-savings-programs).

**What QMB could do for you**
- It can pay your Part B premium. That's the amount taken out of your Social Security each month.
- It can also help with Medicare deductibles, coinsurance and copays.
- Other websites say you'd also get "Extra Help" with prescription costs automatically. I couldn't confirm that on an official page, so ask TennCare.

**Keep in mind**
- Check that the $1,250 is your Social Security **before** the Medicare premium comes out. If it's after, your real income is higher. You'd still probably fit under SLMB or QI, which only pay the Part B premium.
- I can't promise an outcome. TennCare will check your income and savings.
- Full TennCare for people 65 and older has stricter rules, so the Medicare Savings Programs are the better fit. Ask TennCare to check you for every level.

**Next steps**
1. **Apply:** Call TennCare Connect at 855-259-0701, or apply on the TennCare website.
2. **Get free help:** Call 211 for local help. Ask for a SHIP counselor, who can go through the application with you.
3. **Have these handy:** your Medicare card and your Social Security award letter or a recent benefit statement. Bank information may be needed too.
4. **Report everything exactly.** If you're approved based on wrong information, you may have to pay the money back.

I couldn't open TennCare's own website, so please confirm the limits with them when you apply.

Sources:
- [Medicare.gov: Medicare Savings Programs](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/medicare-savings-programs)

Most 2026 sources agree on the Tennessee Medicare Savings Program (MSP) income limits for an individual, but one source gives lower figures, and the Part B premium amounts conflict.

- **Consensus figures (individual, monthly):** Several sources list QMB at $1,350, SLMB at $1,616, and QI at $1,816. Yahoo Finance's federal-guideline breakdown gives the same numbers, and it adds couple limits of $1,824 for QMB, $2,184 for SLMB, and $2,455 for QI. The QMB limit is up to $1,350 for a single person and $1,824 for a married couple. The SLMB limit is up to $1,616 (single) and $2,184 (couple). The QI limit is up to $1,816 (single) and $2,455 (couple).
- **Conflicting figures:** Talk to MIRA gives lower amounts: QMB $1,330, SLMB $1,596, and QI $1,796. Its table lists the same three MSP tiers with those lower single-income amounts and $9,950 in assets. The source doesn't explain the gap, so the lower figures may reflect a different disregard or an older calculation.
- **Assets:** Tennessee uses the federal asset limits: $9,950 for an individual and $14,910 for a couple in 2026.
- **Part B premium:** CoveredUSA says the 2026 premium is $202.90 per month, while other pages list $185.00/month in 2026. The $185 figure is probably the 2025 amount, but I couldn't confirm that from these results.
- **Automatic Extra Help:** Tennessee residents already on full TennCare, SSI, or the TennCare Medicare Savings Program (QMB, SLMB, or QI) are enrolled in Extra Help automatically, with no separate application.
- **Application:** Your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) offers free, unbiased help with MSP applications.

For the official thresholds, check TennCare directly, since most of these figures come from third-party sites.

I didn't find a verified 2026 income limit for TennCare's institutional (nursing home) category or for Medicare Savings Programs, so those figures remain open.

- **Tennessee's coverage structure:** Tennessee hasn't expanded Medicaid, so TennCare covers people 65 or older based on a financial test rather than a flat income cutoff. A 2026 guide says TennCare covers children, pregnant women, people 65 or older or with a disability, and parents and caretakers, with a 2026 Tennessee income chart.
- **Institutional/nursing home Medicaid:** One source describes this as an entitlement; anyone who is eligible will receive assistance. Another says Tennessee's long-term care income limits are higher than the income limit for other TennCare health care benefits. The only dollar figure I found is for 2025, not 2026: a single person could have a monthly income up to $2,901 in 2025, which the source describes as 300% of the SSI 2025 payment level. If that 300% rule still applies, the 2026 figure would be higher, but I couldn't confirm it.
- **Assets:** For people 65 and older, one source says they can have no more than $2,000 in resources and assets (for a household of 1) to qualify for full TennCare coverage.
- **Spousal rules:** When only one spouse applies, the income of the non-applicant spouse doesn't count toward eligibility.
- **Medicare Savings Programs:** I found no 2026 Tennessee figures for these, so I can't confirm the limits.

Sources conflict on exact numbers. The 2022 figures from the older resource pages are outdated, and the 2026 guides mostly cover non-senior groups. Before relying on any figure, check the Division of TennCare's current income chart directly.

input.prompt: What do QMB, SLMB, QI cover and what are the 2026 income and resource limits?

tool_calls.result:
**QMB (Qualified Medicare Beneficiary)** helps pay Part A premiums (if you don't have premium-free Part A), and Part B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and copays for services Medicare covers.

**SLMB (Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary)** helps pay only Part B premiums. You must have both Part A and Part B.

**QI (Qualifying Individual)** helps pay only Part B premiums. You must have both Part A and Part B. You must reapply every year, and approvals are first-come, first-served.

**2026 monthly income and resource limits (federal):**

| Program | Individual income | Individual resources | Married couple income | Married couple resources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QMB | $1,350 | $9,950 | $1,824 | $14,910 |
| SLMB | $1,616 | $9,950 | $2,184 | $14,910 |
| QI | $1,816 | $9,950 | $2,455 | $14,910 |

Income limits are slightly higher in Alaska and Hawaii. Some states use different rules, so you may qualify even above these limits. Contact your state to apply.
